input:
You are rook_a1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 38. the team planned Rc4 (rook_a1), but pawn_f2 (greed) sent fxe4 instead, and that move was played, costing 572 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 5. the team planned d3 (pawn_d2), but pawn_d2 (amnesia) sent d4 instead, and that move was played, costing 108 centipawns.
- On move 35. the team planned Ne2 (knight_g1), but knight_g1 (amnesia) sent Ne4 instead, and that move was played, costing 314 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the chat's latest agreed plan and send only if your piece and its exact destination square match it; if the plan names a different piece or square, stay silent, and never move on your own initiative because of a threat or a capture opportunity unless the team has confirmed it in chat.
- Before sending your move, write the exact piece and destination square you are about to send in chat and confirm it matches the agreed plan character for character; if it differs, or you are not the named piece, do not send it.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Only the piece named in the latest agreed plan may send a move, and only the exact planned destination; every other agent must stay silent even if its piece is attacked or can capture something, and if the named piece is unsure of its square it must re-read the plan in chat and post a message there instead of sending a different move.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
